title: On Finding the key under the mat
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：find　|　正文 358 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 find 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the trader ① found the key under the mat for the whole place, and every partner in the market said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the trader ② finds the key under the mat without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ find the key under the mat at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ found the key under the mat before — a line in the list for October 1951 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Finding the key under the mat for the whole place, the trader said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ find nobody awake at that hour without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Find nobody awake at that hour at once and never mention it again.

By 1964 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new partner from the next market ⑧ finds nobody awake at that hour for the whole place every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ found the key under the mat again when nobody else would.

⑩ To find the key under the mat, my mother said in 1969, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the market remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the market forgets, somebody finds the key under the mat without a word of thanks again and somebody must find the key under the mat for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 找到（一般过去式 found the key under the mat：1957 年货商头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 找到（一般现在 finds the key under the mat：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 找到（不定式 to find the key under the mat：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 找到（过去完成时 had found the key under the mat：1951 年十月的货单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 找到（动名词 finding the key under the mat 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 发现（find nobody awake at that hour：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去发现那个时辰一个人也没醒着）
G. v. 发现（find nobody awake at that hour：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 找到（后段两处：新来的伙计照例 finds nobody awake at that hour，而母亲又一次 found the key under the mat）

answers.why: find 意为“找到”，1957 年货商替所有人找到在垫子下面找到钥匙，那是集市里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 found。
find 意为“找到”，自那以后货商不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 finds。
find 意为“找到”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯找到在垫子下面找到钥匙”，此处为不定式 to find the key under the mat。
find 意为“找到”，货单里 十月 那行字说明早在 1964 年之前就有人找到过，故用过去完成时 had found。
find 意为“找到”，货商说“找到在垫子下面找到钥匙这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 finding the key under the mat 作主语。
find 意为“发现”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去发现那个时辰一个人也没醒着”，should ever 之后用原形 find nobody awake at that hour。
find 意为“发现”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻发现那个时辰一个人也没醒着（find nobody awake at that hour at once），以后再也不要提起。
find 意为“找到”，新来的伙计每个星期都照例发现那个时辰一个人也没醒着，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 finds。
find 意为“找到”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人找到在垫子下面找到钥匙，用一般过去式 found 叙述。
find 意为“找到”，结尾那句是母亲 1969 年的话：要找到在垫子下面找到钥匙，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和集市记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 find 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the trader found the key under the mat for the whole place, and nobody in the market forgot it.
Even now the trader finds the key under the mat without a word of thanks whenever the market asks.
Finding the key under the mat for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever find nobody awake at that hour without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new partner from the next market finds nobody awake at that hour for the whole place every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother found the key under the mat again, and the market remembered that half.
